newsitem.title: POLAND: Weimar ministers urge peaceful end to Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Weimar ministers urge peaceful end to Peru crisis.

text.p: Foreign ministers of France, Germany and Poland, meeting in Warsaw on Thursday, urged Peru's government to end the Lima hostage crisis without bloodshed.

"We would like to urge the Peruvian government to do all it can to save lives of the hostages," German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said after the annual meeting of the three ministers from the so-called Weimar triangle countries.

Leftist guerrillas, holding up to 484 people including high-ranking diplomats, businessmen and government officials at the Japanese ambassador's residence, demanded the release of 400 to 500 jailed comrades and the presence of President Alberto Fujimori for talks.
Kinkel told a news conference that he had contacted the German ambassador to Lima, among five diplomats released by the rebels on Wednesday, who told him the guerrillas were heavily armed.
"The terrorists are heavily armed...and they persist in their demands," he said.
They threaten to kill the hostages if their demands are not met.
Kinkel said the ambassador had told him the hostages were held by 18 guerrillas, one of whom had been wounded.
Kinkel and his French and Polish counterparts, Herve de Charette and Dariusz Rosati, met to discuss the enlargement of the European Union and NATO.
They confirmed that Poland, along with other countries of the former Soviet bloc, should start EU membership negotiations in early 1998.
